items.item: The header shows the delivery note number, issue date, source sales order or transfer number and dispatching warehouse, each with a visible label, and every date on the note uses one unambiguous format (such as 06 Nov 2026)
items.evidence: Header identity block (lines 61-66) only has 'Delivery note no.', 'Order reference', 'Date issued', 'Dispatch date' — the dispatching warehouse ('Central DC — Unit 12') lives only in the separate 'Shipment details' section below, not the header. Also dates are rendered by fmtDate with Intl options {day:'2-digit', month:'2-digit', year:'numeric'} producing '07/11/2026' — an all-numeric DD/MM/YYYY string, not the unambiguous 'DD Mon YYYY' format the checklist requires.

items.item: Sender (company name, address, tax ID), recipient (customer name, delivery address, contact person and phone) and carrier (carrier name, vehicle plate or driver name) appear in three separately labelled blocks
items.evidence: There is a labelled 'Sender' block (h2#h-sender) with name/address/Tax ID, but recipient data is split across two separate blocks — 'Customer' (section aria-labelledby=h-customer, name/tax ID/contact/phone) and 'Deliver to' (section aria-labelledby=h-shipto, delivery address). Carrier info ('Swift Freight Solutions', 'LD19 KXP', 'Marcus Webb') has no block of its own at all — it is just two <dt>/<dd> fields inside the unrelated 'Shipment details' box (h2#h-shipment) mixed with Warehouse.

items.item: The goods are in a real <table> with column headers in <thead>, giving per line: line number, item code, description, unit of measure, quantity ordered, quantity delivered and lot or serial number, with quantities right-aligned
items.evidence: <table> with <thead> columns are No., Item, SKU, Unit, Qty ordered, Qty shipped, Notes (lines 120-129) — quantities use class 'text-right' correctly, but there is no lot/serial number column; 'Notes' is a free-text remark field, not a lot/serial field.

items.item: A line delivered short of the ordered quantity states the outstanding amount in words (such as "Backorder: 4 pcs") rather than by colour alone
items.evidence: Line 3 (Safety gloves, ordered 30 / shipped 28) carries note text '2 boxes on backorder' in the Notes column (lines[2].note, rendered in <td> at line 245) — the 2-unit shortfall is stated in words, no colour-only signal is used.

items.item: A footer gives the total quantity delivered, the number of packages and the gross weight with its unit, and the quantity total equals the sum of the lines
items.evidence: <tfoot id="totals"> only sums 'Qty ordered' (268) and 'Qty shipped' (266 = 12+2+28+200+24, correctly matching the line sum) — there is no package count or gross-weight figure anywhere on the page.

items.item: Signature boxes are provided for the warehouse keeper (issued by), the driver or carrier and the receiver, each with room for printed name, signature and date, plus a remarks area for the condition of the goods on receipt
items.evidence: Three boxes exist — 'Prepared by' (Warehouse), 'Delivered by' (Driver/carrier), 'Received by' (Customer) — each with Name/Signature/Date fields (lines 152-201). However there is no remarks/condition-on-receipt field anywhere in the signatures section; only a generic sentence 'the customer confirms the goods listed above were received in the condition noted' with no blank area to actually record that condition.

items.item: A Print control that is a real <button> starts printing, and an @media print stylesheet hides the app navigation and on-screen controls, sets page margins and keeps the signature block from splitting across pages
items.evidence: <button type="button" id="btn-print">Print</button> wired to `$('btn-print').addEventListener('click', () => window.print())`; @media print rule `.no-print, [role="status"] { display: none !important; }` hides the breadcrumb nav and on-screen buttons; `@page { size: A4; margin: 14mm 12mm 16mm; }` sets margins; `.signatures { break-inside: avoid; }` keeps the signature block intact across pages.

items.item: The note's status (such as Draft, Dispatched, Delivered or Cancelled) is shown in words next to its number, and a draft or cancelled note prints with a visible "DRAFT" or "CANCELLED" mark so it cannot pass as a valid dispatch document
items.evidence: Status is shown in words next to the number: `Shipped` beside the h1 'Delivery note · DN-2026-04821'. But the status is hardcoded to 'Shipped' with no Draft/Cancelled state or any print watermark logic in the script — there is no mechanism that would stamp a DRAFT or CANCELLED mark when printed.

items.item: A loading state is present, and a note that fails to load or does not exist shows a message with Retry and a link back to the delivery note list, never an empty template with blank fields
items.evidence: The script immediately calls `render()` on a hardcoded `doc`/`lines` object (lines 217-261) with no loading indicator, no fetch/error branch, and no Retry/back-to-list UI anywhere in the markup or script.

notes: Page is a static mock (hardcoded doc/lines data, no fetch), so loading/error/draft-cancelled states are unimplemented by construction. Main structural gaps vs. checklist: no lot/serial column, no package-count/gross-weight footer, no remarks-on-receipt field, warehouse missing from header, carrier lacks its own labelled block, and dates use an ambiguous numeric DD/MM/YYYY format instead of 'DD Mon YYYY'. Audit.json reports score 100/100 with no automated violations, underscoring that these are semantic/content gaps the automated linter does not check. 'card-in-card' tell: the outer .sheet card (rounded-md border bg-white p-8) nests multiple further bordered rounded-md boxes (Shipment details, each signature box, the Notes box) inside it.
